description: Split the opaque Integrate integrate:merge delivery into two real, ordered tasks — integrate:prepare (rebase + first-class conflict resolution) and integrate:publish (land one commit + push) — with classified, recoverable delivery failures.

tasks.title: Implement split delivery runner actions (mohist/prepare + mohist/publish) and remove mohist/merge
tasks.spec: specs/merge-delivery/spec.md#Integrate delivery is prepare then publish
tasks.description: In packages/runner/src/actions, add prepareAction: operate in the issue worktree (context.workDir where mo/issue-N is HEAD), fetch the latest base, rebase the issue branch onto it, and reuse the existing rebase.ts conflict-resolution machinery (runConflictResolver, verifyRebaseComplete, abortRebaseIfInProgress) so conflict resolution is the task's visible work with its own attempts/evidence. Add publishAction: operate in project.path, checkout base, git merge --squash the prepared issue branch into a single commit, then git push it to the remote; it MUST contain no agent conflict-resolution loop. Emit a structured failureKind in each action's output JSON (conflict from prepare; base-moved on squash conflict or non-fast-forward push; retry-safe for transient errors). Guarantee a clean workspace on failure (rebase --abort for prepare; merge --abort / reset base for publish). Register mohist/prepare and mohist/publish in createDefaultRegistry(), delete mergeAction and the mohist/merge registration, and replace tests/merge.spec.ts with tests/prepare.spec.ts and tests/publish.spec.ts reusing the injectable git/resolver test harness.
acceptanceCriteria: prepareAction rebases mo/issue-N onto the fetched base branch and records preparedBaseSha and the prepared candidate head in its output

prepareAction resolves conflicts via the reused rebase conflict-resolution path and reports failureKind 'conflict' when a conflict cannot be resolved, with git rebase --abort leaving no rebase in progress
publishAction lands the issue changes as exactly one commit on the base branch in project.path and pushes it to the remote, recording the landed commit and that the push occurred
publishAction performs no agent conflict-resolution loop; when the base moved it reports failureKind 'base-moved' and restores the base branch to its pre-publish state with no partial commit
transient publish failures report failureKind 'retry-safe'; only publish ever runs git push
mohist/merge and mergeAction are removed; createDefaultRegistry() registers mohist/prepare and mohist/publish
prepare.spec.ts and publish.spec.ts pass, asserting the exact git call sequences and the parsed output shape including failureKind; merge.spec.ts is deleted
tasks.output: packages/runner/src/actions/registry.ts (+ reused exports from rebase.ts), packages/runner/tests/prepare.spec.ts, packages/runner/tests/publish.spec.ts
tasks.notes: Linked worktrees share the project repo refs, so publish in project.path sees the mo/issue-N ref that prepare rebased in the issue worktree — add a test asserting this. Keep the closed failureKind set aligned with specs/merge-delivery/spec.md.

tasks.title: Switch the default Integrate stage to integrate:prepare then integrate:publish
tasks.spec: specs/workflow-definition/spec.md#REQ-WD-002 Integrate uses the standard task/check stage contract
tasks.description: Update packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Issue/Services/WorkflowProfiles/mohist-default.workflow.yaml: replace the single integrate:merge (mohist/merge) task with integrate:prepare (mohist/prepare, baseBranch from project.baseBranch, with a conflictResolver titled 'Resolve prepare conflicts') followed by integrate:publish (mohist/publish, source mo/issue-${{ issue.number }}, target project.baseBranch, message 'Complete issue #${{ issue.number }}'). Preserve the integrate:spec-sync then integrate:archive-change ordering ahead of delivery, and keep the health check, lockBehavior: sequential, and project-integration resource unchanged. Align workflow-run delivery/freeze facts and the post-publish-health-failed reason with the prepare+publish split.
acceptanceCriteria: mohist-default.workflow.yaml declares integrate:prepare then integrate:publish in that order, after integrate:archive-change, using mohist/prepare and mohist/publish respectively
integrate:spec-sync precedes integrate:archive-change which precedes integrate:prepare which precedes integrate:publish
the Integrate health check, lockBehavior: sequential, and project-integration resource are unchanged
the default workflow loads/validates without errors (existing workflow-definition tests pass)
no code or config references the removed mohist/merge action, integrate:merge task, or post-merge-health-failed reason
tasks.notes: The server binds Integrate tasks generically from the yaml, so no server domain-model change is expected beyond the yaml; verify by loading the default workflow profile.

tasks.title: Surface delivery failure kinds in the CLI and Web UI
tasks.spec: specs/merge-delivery/spec.md#Delivery failures are classified into actionable kinds
tasks.description: Render the prepare/publish failureKind (conflict, base-moved, retry-safe) and its recommended next action wherever failed Integrate delivery task results are shown: the CLI task-failure output and the Web task/log surfaces. Reuse the existing structured task-result output channel — do not introduce a new transport or domain event. Map each failureKind to the corresponding guidance (conflict -> needs attention; base-moved -> prepare again then publish; retry-safe -> just retry).
acceptanceCriteria: CLI delivery task failure output includes the failureKind and the recommended next action
Web task/log surface displays the failureKind and recommended next action for failed prepare/publish tasks
failureKind rendering relies on the existing task-result output payload; no new realtime channel or domain event is added
unit/component tests cover the failureKind-to-guidance mapping for all three kinds in both CLI and Web
tasks.output: CLI failure-rendering path, Web task/log failure-rendering components, and their tests
tasks.notes: Scope is limited to displaying the kind already emitted by the runner actions; keep the CLI/Web change proportional and do not build new failure infrastructure.
